name: DRV8231ADSGR
title: DRV8231A: 3.7 A brushed DC motor H-bridge, 4.5 V to 33 V, with current-mirror sensing (IPROPI) and current regulation
summary: A single full bridge of four N-channel MOSFETs (about 300 mΩ each side) for one brushed DC motor, a relay coil or another inductive load, running from 4.5 V to 33 V on one supply pin with an internal charge pump for the high-side gates. Two logic inputs, IN1 and IN2, select forward, reverse, brake or coast and accept PWM up to 200 kHz; holding both low puts the chip to sleep below 1 µA. A mirror on the low-side FETs sources 1500 µA per amp of load current out of IPROPI, so a resistor there gives a voltage for an ADC, and comparing that voltage with VREF chops the bridge at a set current with a fixed 25 µs off time. Undervoltage lockout, auto-retry overcurrent and thermal shutdown are built in. Packages: 8-pin HSOP PowerPAD (DDA) and 2 mm × 2 mm 8-pin WSON (DSG).

pins.name: IPROPI
pins.function: Sources a current proportional to the low-side FET current (AIPROPI, 1500 µA/A). A resistor to ground turns it into a voltage that also sets the regulation trip against VREF. Tie to GND to turn off regulation and feedback.

pins.name: IN2
pins.function: Bridge control input with internal pulldown (100 kΩ typ). With IN1 it selects the output state in the bridge control table.

pins.name: IN1
pins.function: Bridge control input with internal pulldown (100 kΩ typ). With IN2 it selects the output state in the bridge control table.

pins.name: VREF
pins.function: Reference for the current regulation threshold, 0 V to 3.6 V recommended (6 V absolute maximum). Also the level the IPROPI clamp follows.

pins.name: VM
pins.function: Supply for the device and the motor, 4.5 V to 33 V recommended. Bypass to ground with 0.1 µF ceramic plus bulk capacitance, all rated for VM.

pins.name: OUT1

pins.name: GND
pins.function: Power ground of the device; tie to system ground.

pins.name: OUT2
pins.function: Bridge output; wire straight to the other terminal of the motor or load.

pins.name: PAD
pins.function: Exposed thermal pad. Solder to board ground; large ground planes on several layers joined by many vias near the pad carry the heat away.

circuits.title: Typical connections: brushed DC motor
circuits.description: One brushed DC motor between OUT1 and OUT2, run from a 4.5 V to 33 V supply on VM with a 0.1 µF ceramic and a 47 µF bulk capacitor to ground. A controller on 3.3 V drives IN1 and IN2 and reads the IPROPI voltage across RIPROPI with its ADC. VREF sits on 3.3 V, so the bridge chops when the IPROPI voltage reaches 3.3 V; with 1.5 kΩ that is about 1.46 A.

parts.note: IPROPI sense resistance from the design parameters

circuits.title: Single-coil latching relay driving
circuits.description: The coil of a single-coil latching relay sits across OUT1 and OUT2, so forward and reverse drive set and reset it. Two controller PWM outputs drive IN1 and IN2; VREF is tied to the 3.3 V logic supply VCC and IPROPI has its resistor to ground. VM takes a 0.1 µF bypass and a bulk capacitor. Example coil current is a 500 mA pulse for 200 ms from a 12 V VM.
notes: After the pulse the outputs can go to sleep (IN1 = IN2 = 0) or brake briefly so the coil's stored energy does not flow back into VM.

circuits.title: Dual-coil latching relay driving
circuits.description: A dual-coil latching relay has its centre tap on VM and one coil end on each output. Driving OUT1 low energises Coil1 while OUT2 rises to VM so Coil2 carries nothing; the opposite state drives Coil2. Only the low-side FETs do work, and the high-side body diodes catch the coil current, so no extra freewheeling diodes are fitted. Example coil current is a 100 mA pulse for 200 ms.

parts.note: COIL1 end, centre tap CT, COIL2 end

circuits.title: IPROPI sensing on a footprint shared with shunt-sense drivers
circuits.description: Board option that takes either the DRV8231A or a shunt-sense part on the same pinout. Fitted for the DRV8231A: pin 1 carries IPROPI into a 1.5 kΩ resistor to ground and through 0 Ω to the ADC line, and a 0 Ω link joins pin 7 to ground. The sense amplifier and its output resistor are not fitted; they serve the shunt-sense part, where pin 7 is the sense node.
notes: Misprint in the pin labels: pin 2 is IN2 and pin 3 is IN1.

For the shunt-sense parts (DRV8870, DRV8231, DRV8251) pin 1 is GND, pin 7 is ISEN with a 0.5 Ω Rsense to ground, the sense amplifier output goes through 0 Ω to the ADC line and the 1.5 kΩ position is 0 Ω to ground with the series position not fitted.

operation.text: One supply pin, VM, feeds both the logic and the motor. An internal charge pump lifts the high-side gate drive above VM so all four FETs are N-channel and 100 % duty cycle is possible. The bridge totals about 600 mΩ (one high-side plus one low-side FET). PWM from 0 to 200 kHz sets speed.

Static levels on IN1 and IN2 give full drive; PWM gives variable speed. Alternating drive with brake (for forward, IN1 held high and IN2 toggled) is the usual PWM pattern; drive alternating with coast (both low) gives fast decay instead. The inputs may be driven before VM comes up.

Each change of an output between high and low inserts dead time (tDEAD, 200 ns typ) with the output High-Z to stop shoot-through. During it the output sits a diode drop below ground if current leaves the pin, or a diode drop above VM if current enters it, through a FET body diode. tPD runs from an input edge to the output change and includes an input deglitch filter; the FET switching adds tRISE and tFALL.

A current mirror on each low-side FET feeds IPROPI, so no power shunt is needed. Current is seen in drive and in brake (slow decay), so a bidirectional brushed motor can be monitored continuously. In coast the current freewheels source to drain and is not seen; it can be sampled by briefly switching back to drive or brake. AERR combines the mirror's gain error and an offset added to the load current. Size RIPROPI so the expected load current fills the ADC range. An internal clamp limits VIPROPI relative to VREF to protect the ADC during overcurrent.

IPROPI is ready tDELAY (1.1 µs typ) after the inputs turn a low-side FET on. In drive/brake PWM the sensing FET stays on and this delay does not matter. When the inputs turn the low-side FETs off, IPROPI stops at once, even though the FET keeps conducting while it slews off.

An internal comparator compares VIPROPI with VVREF. When the load current passes ITRIP, the bridge brakes (both low-side FETs on) for tOFF (25 µs typ), then returns to the input state if the current has fallen below ITRIP, or brakes for another tOFF if not. No new input edge is needed, so regulation works at 100 % duty. A change on IN1 or IN2 during tOFF ends it early and the outputs follow the inputs. Blanking (tBLK) after switching and deglitching (tDEG) keep transients, for example from a capacitor in or across the motor, from tripping it; for longer transients a 10 nF capacitor from IPROPI to ground close to the device filters them, at the cost of slower regulation response. VVREF must stay in its recommended range.
Tie IPROPI to GND with VREF above GND to turn off both regulation and feedback. For feedback without regulation, choose VVREF and RIPROPI so VIPROPI never reaches VVREF.

Each FET has an analog current limit that clamps its gate drive. If the limit lasts beyond tOCP (1.5 µs typ) the whole bridge turns off and retries after tRETRY (3 ms typ), repeating while the fault stays. High- and low-side FETs are watched separately, so shorts to ground, to supply or across the load all trip it. OCP does not use the IPROPI sense path and works whatever VREF and IPROPI are set to.
Above TTSD the bridge turns off; it restarts on its own once the die has cooled by THYS.
When VM falls below the UVLO falling threshold, the outputs and all circuitry turn off and the logic resets. Operation resumes when VM rises above the rising threshold.

The device is active once VM is above VUVLO, an input is high and tWAKE (250 µs max) has passed. With IN1 and IN2 both low for tSLEEP the device sleeps with outputs High-Z and draws IVMQ; powered up with both inputs low it sleeps at once. Either input held high longer than tWAKE wakes it.
IN1 and IN2 each have a 100 kΩ pulldown to ground.

Higher VM spins the motor faster at a given duty and raises the rate of current change in the winding. Current peaks at start-up, low speed and stall; the internal regulation can cap the inrush, or the controller can ramp the PWM duty at start.

Motor current rises at stall, from a jam or an end stop. The controller reads VIPROPI with an ADC (or a comparator) against a firmware threshold placed between the average running current and the stall current. It ignores readings above threshold during the start-up inrush time tINRUSH, found by test, and acts after the current has stayed high for tSTALL: long to let the motor clear a jam, short at an end stop to save power and gears.

Forward or reverse drive sets or resets a single-coil latching relay. Afterwards the inputs can go low to sleep, or the bridge can brake briefly so back EMF from the coil does not push current into VM. Current regulation can hold the coil current within its rating when VM exceeds the relay voltage.

The bulk capacitor on VM depends on the peak motor current, the supply's capacitance and current capability, the wiring inductance to the supply, allowed ripple, motor type and braking method. Too little and VM swings with motor current demand and with energy returned by the motor. The final value comes from system testing. Rate the capacitor above the operating voltage to leave room for energy the motor sends back.

Use a low-ESR X5R or X7R ceramic from VM to GND and keep it and the bulk capacitor (ceramic or electrolytic) right beside the device so the current loop stays small. VM, OUT1, OUT2 and GND carry the load current and want wide copper. Join the thermal pad to the top ground plane and inner ground planes with thermal vias and give it as much copper as possible.

RθJA depends strongly on the board: stack-up, vias, and copper round the pad. Both RθJA and ΨJB fall as the board gains copper area, layer count or copper weight. For short pulses (start-up, a shorted output tripping OCP, brief solenoid or motor drive) die and package dominate and the thermal impedance ZθJA is much lower; for long pulses the board dominates and the result approaches steady state. Measurement in the system is more reliable than the estimates.

The DRV8231A shares its pinout and footprint with the DRV8251A. The DDA footprint also matches the shunt-sense DRV8870, DRV8251 and DRV8231, whose pin 1 is GND and pin 7 the sense node; one board can carry either kind by fitting or omitting a few resistors and the sense amplifier.
